physics-killer-08.title: Newton's Laws of Motion and Special Relativity
physics-killer-08.topic: Newton's Laws of Motion and Special Relativity
physics-killer-08.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
physics-killer-08.material: A muon produced in the upper atmosphere travels vertically downward toward the ground at speed $0.8c$. In the Earth (ground) frame the production point is at a height of $800\,\mathrm{m}$, and the muon's mean lifetime measured in its own rest frame is $2.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. With $c=3\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}$, which option correctly gives, in order, the distance from the production point to the ground as seen in the muon's rest frame and the time the muon takes to cover that distance?
physics-killer-08.thinking.0: Newton's Laws of Motion and Special Relativity
physics-killer-08.s.s1.prompt: A muon produced in the upper atmosphere travels vertically downward toward the ground at speed $0.8c$. In the Earth (ground) frame the production point is at a height of $800\,\mathrm{m}$, and the muon's mean lifetime measured in its own rest frame is $2.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. With $c=3\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}$, which option correctly gives, in order, the distance from the production point to the ground as seen in the muon's rest frame and the time the muon takes to cover that distance?
physics-killer-08.s.s1.explain: $\gamma=1/\sqrt{1-0.8^2}=5/3$. Length contraction: $L=L_0/\gamma=800\cdot\dfrac35=480\,\mathrm{m}$. Time $t=\dfrac{L}{v}=\dfrac{480}{0.8\cdot3\times10^8}=2.0\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{s}=2.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}$, equal to the muon's proper lifetime. The Earth observer explains the same event by time dilation: $\Delta t=\dfrac{800}{0.8c}=3.3\,\mu\mathrm{s}=\gamma\cdot2.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Multiplying by $\gamma$ gives $1333\,\mathrm{m}$ (option 1), multiplying by $v/c$ instead gives $640\,\mathrm{m}$ (option 2), and ignoring contraction gives option 4.
physics-killer-08.s.s2.prompt: Which scenario demonstrates the correct real-world application of this principle?
physics-killer-08.s.s2.explain: The fundamental principles of this inquiry are widely implemented in modern technology.

With $c=3\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}$, which option correctly gives, in order, the distance from the production point to the ground as seen in the muon's rest frame and the time the muon takes to cover that distance?

The Earth observer explains the same event by time dilation: $\Delta t=\dfrac{800}{0.8c}=3.3\,\mu\mathrm{s}=\gamma\cdot2.0\,\mu\mathrm{s}$. Multiplying by $\gamma$ gives $1333\,\mathrm{m}$ (option 1), multiplying by $v/c$ instead gives $640\,\mathrm{m}$ (option 2), and ignoring contraction gives option 4.
